description:
About the Position

The Department of Meteorology at Stockholm University invites applications for a PhD student position in atmospheric sciences and oceanography, focused on mixed-phase cloud processes. Mixed-phase clouds - containing both supercooled liquid water and ice - control cloud lifetime and radiative effect in cold regions, and their representation remains a challenge for weather and climate models. The doctoral project studies ice nucleation, secondary ice production and cloud glaciation using a combination of observations and cloud-resolving modelling, within a salaried four-year employment under the Swedish collective agreement.

The department's cloud group participates in Nordic and Arctic measurement campaigns and maintains collaborations across the European cloud-research community. Doctoral researchers are trained in cloud microphysics, instrumentation and numerical experimentation, and the Stockholm environment offers access to high-performance computing, national observation infrastructure and seminar networks spanning the atmospheric and climate sciences.

Candidate Profile

Applicants hold a master's degree in meteorology, physics or a related discipline, with strong quantitative skills and interest in cloud microphysics. Experience with field measurements, radar or satellite data, or cloud modelling is an advantage. Applications are made through the Varbi recruitment system with CV, transcripts, references and a statement of interest.

Highlights

  • PhD on mixed-phase cloud processes at Stockholm MISU
  • Ice nucleation, secondary ice and glaciation research
  • Observations plus cloud-resolving modelling
  • Nordic and Arctic campaign participation
  • Salaried four-year employment per Swedish collective agreement
  • Application via the Varbi recruitment system

About Stockholm University

Stockholm University is a public research university in the Swedish capital with roughly 30,000 students and a strong research profile in the natural sciences, psychology, humanities, law and social sciences. Many of its departments collaborate with national research institutes located on the same campus areas, including the neighbouring Science for Life Laboratory environment. Doctoral students in Sweden are employed on paid contracts with collective-agreement salaries and full social benefits. PhD and postdoctoral vacancies are recruited through the national Varbi system used by Swedish universities.
